description: Debt-backlog record — a queued structural/technical-debt entry, one YAML file per entry under state/debt-backlog/<date>-<slug>.yaml (whole-document YAML; no prose markdown body). additionalProperties-posture: open — unknown fields in debt-backlog records are tolerated (not rejected). This preserves forward-compatibility as new optional fields are added without invalidating existing records. Decision: keep open; tighten only if strict-mode corpus conformance enforcement is required at a future governance stage.
_additionalProperties_note: Permissive by design — additionalProperties is not set to false here, consistent with the handoff/goal schemas. A misspelled field will silently pass. This is intentional for forward-compatibility and matches the existing permissive pattern in other coordinator schemas.

created.description: Date this debt-backlog entry was authored (YYYY-MM-DD).

title.description: Short business-legible title for this debt entry.

body.description: Prose description of the debt — what it is and why it matters.

status.description: Lifecycle status. open=unresolved; closed=resolved (git mv to archive/debt-backlog/<YYYY-MM>/ on closure); deferred=explicitly deprioritized.

source.description: Where this debt entry originated (e.g. a review finding, an audit, a session observation).

risk.description: Prose statement of the risk this debt poses if left unaddressed.

proposed_action.description: Prose statement of the recommended remediation.

from_repo.description: Originating repo, when the debt entry was raised cross-repo.

surface.description: The code/doc surface this debt entry concerns.

closed_at.description: Date this debt entry was closed (YYYY-MM-DD). Present only once status transitions to closed.

closed_by.description: Session or agent identifier that closed this entry.

evidence.description: Supporting evidence for the debt claim (file:line, log excerpt, link).

severity.description: Priority severity of the debt entry, P0 highest.

initiative.description: FK to state/initiatives/<id>.yaml; nullable — absent≡null. Spec backlink: pln-initiative-govern-sweep-priori-6cf808 § C0

created_by_session.description: Session identifier that authored this entry.

created_by_agent.description: Agent type that authored this entry.

linked_sessions.description: Session identifiers linked to this entry's history.

linked_commits.description: Commit SHAs linked to this entry's history.

provenance_completeness.description: Whether the provenance chain (session/agent/commits) is fully recorded or unknown.

pm_approved.description: Records that the PM gate authorising this deferral fired. For a ceremony park (/debt-triage Step 6b class 4) the ceremony asserts its own gate; it is not a second approval act by the PM. No ceremony parks bug rows today -- /bug-blitz has no park step -- so a deferred bug row is hand-authored: the author RECORDS a grant the PM gave, and never grants it themselves. Same field name as plan-tasks.schema.json's shipped gate -- one vocabulary across surfaces, deliberately. Boolean, not the PM's words -- a date or a quote here is schema-invalid and refuses at the step that reads it; put what was said in `why_blocked` or `body` (tripwire PM-APPROVED-IS-A-BOOLEAN-NOT-THE-PMS-WORDS).

deferred_by.description: Who granted the deferral: for a ceremony park, the ceremony identifier plus the session that ran it. Mirrors closed_by. For a hand-authored park, name the granting authority and when -- never the authoring session. A sibling deny refuses a `deferred_by` that names the record's own author, and that refusal is correct: this field answers who authorised the park, not who typed it.

deferred_until.description: ISO date the deferral expires. Its presence is what makes a due-list a read of grants rather than a corpus scan; its absence is how a parked record drifts unnoticed.

why_blocked.description: Why this entry is deferred. Required in doctrine whenever status=deferred.

case_against.description: OPTIONAL. The argument that lost -- so a triager sees both the case for doing the work (proposed_action/body) and the case against it. Mirrors improvement-queue.schema.json's field of the same name, added here so the three backlog families stop disagreeing on a property one of them already had. It MUST stay optional at the top level even though the deferred-grant branch requires it: an omitted field says nothing was carried, while an empty string asserts there was no argument, and a hand-authored row that was never a plan deferral has nothing to carry.

allOf.$comment: Cross-field rule: a deferral is a GRANT, not a state. When `status` is `deferred` the four grant fields plus `case_against` must be PRESENT. Presence, not truthiness -- a row with `pm_approved: false` or a blank `why_blocked` still validates here; this schema does not hard-fail it. The truthiness floor (pm_approved must be literal true, non-blank case_against/why_blocked, parseable deferred_until, non-empty deferred_by) lives in claude-klabauter's schema_validate.py cross-field rule, and refusal lives in their write guard. Reading this branch as the enforcement point is the misread the $comment exists to prevent. Shape copied from plan-tasks.schema.json's own allOf[0], on claude-klabauter-em's ask (cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-28-claude-klabauter-em-queue-deferral-grant-conditional-on-the-three-backlog-schemas.md) -- they cannot author it locally without tripping three vendor-drift gates.

then.$comment: Presence-only, per the branch $comment above. Required here so a deferral cannot be asserted without naming who granted it, until when, what the argument against was, and what is blocking.

x-bump-note: 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0 adds the status:deferred conditional the four grant fields existed for but nothing tied together, plus case_against where it was missing. Requested by claude-klabauter-em, who cannot author it in their vendored copy: a shape change under an unmoved x-schema-version is red on their parity test, check_schema_drift byte-compares against a pinned DoE ref, and the consumer-ahead gate blocks a local bump. Presence-only by contract -- truthiness and refusal are theirs. Zero records in either tree carry status: deferred today (727 measured across the three DoE queues), so nothing existing is invalidated. ON THE CLASS, corrected after review: this is recorded `major`, not `nested-field-additive` as first committed at 17e73ce67. The additive test is 'every document valid under the prior version still validates', and this bump FAILS it -- a row carrying `status: deferred` and none of the grant fields validated at the prior version and does not validate here. That is the whole point of the branch. The vocabulary in docs/wiki/schema-version-gate.md offers no `narrowing` term (`major`, `nested-field-additive`, `enum-value-additive`, `top-level-array-additive`), so this follows peer-set-entry.schema.json's precedent for a change none of the four describes: take the nearest fit on the SAFE side, since over-stating the duty makes a vendoring sibling wait longer than needed while under-stating it lets them skip a hold they owed. NO document is actually invalidated -- 727 records measured across the three DoE queues and claude-klabauter's own count, zero carrying `status: deferred` in either tree -- so the narrowing is real in the schema and empty in the corpus. `major`'s hold duty is DISCHARGED rather than skipped: claude-klabauter-em asked for this exact shape, has accepted the re-vendor leg via bin/claude-klabauter-revendor-schema.py, and is the only sibling vendoring it. Bilateral sequencing is what the hold exists to arrange, and it was arranged before the bump.
